content.text:
My investigation is complete. The termination architecture fully meets our preferred position:

- **§ 9.4** gives Customer an unrestricted convenience right ("without cause") over the Agreement or any Order Form, with only accrued Fees owed and a refund of prepaid Fees for the post-termination period (pro-rata refund).
- **§ 29.4** sets that notice period at exactly thirty days — matching our preferred 30 days, so the cross-reference resolves favourably rather than hiding a longer period.
- **§ 10.2** reinforces the prepaid-fee refund on termination.
- **No early-termination fee or penalty** exists anywhere (§ 7 contains no termination charge; § 7.6 blocks unidentified charges; the only liquidated-damages clause in § 7.7 relates to late invoice payment, which is outside this rule's scope).
- **Vendor has no convenience right.** Its only termination rights are mutual: material breach (§ 9.1) and insolvency (§ 9.2). Searches for "Vendor may terminate", "convenience", and "without cause" return no Vendor discretionary exit, and § 20.5 (p0087) and § 24.4 (p0102) affirmatively restrain Vendor from terminating unaffected Services or terminating on Customer change of control.

Since the clause already achieves the preferred position, no redline is warranted.

input.quote: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form without cause by delivering the written notice specified in Section 29.4. Customer owes only accrued Fees, and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the period after termination.
input.rationale: Meets the preferred position in full. Section 9.4 grants Customer a convenience ("without cause") termination right over the Agreement or any individual Order Form, limits Customer's exposure to accrued Fees only, and requires Vendor to refund prepaid Fees for the post-termination period (a pro-rata refund, reinforced by Section 10.2). The notice period is supplied by cross-reference to Section 29.4, which resolves to thirty days before the effective termination date — exactly the preferred 30 days. No early-termination fee, penalty, or acceleration attaches: searches for "early termination", "penalty", and "remainder of the term" surface nothing applicable, and Section 7.6 bars charges not identified in the Order Form (the Section 7.7 liquidated-damages provision is a late-invoice-payment matter outside this rule). On direction, Vendor has no convenience right during the three-year term (Section 8.1): its only termination rights are the mutual ones for uncured material breach (Section 9.1) and insolvency (Section 9.2), and searches for "Vendor may terminate", "convenience", and "without cause" return no Vendor discretionary exit. Sections 20.5 and 24.4 further restrain Vendor from terminating unaffected Services or terminating on a Customer change of control. No redline needed.
